items.prompt: Read: 'The enormous elephant could not fit through the door.' Enormous means — (A) very large  (B) very small

steps: The elephant cannot fit through the door, so it must be very large.
Enormous means very large.

items.prompt: Read: 'The fragile vase broke when it was dropped.' Fragile means — (A) very heavy  (B) easily broken

steps: The vase broke when dropped, which tells us it breaks easily.
Fragile means easily broken.

items.prompt: The word unhappy has the prefix un-. Unhappy means — (A) not happy  (B) very happy

steps: The prefix un- means 'not.'
un- + happy = not happy.

items.prompt: Read: 'Please retell the story to your friend.' Retell means — (A) listen to a story  (B) tell a story again

steps: The prefix re- means 'again.'
retell = tell again.

items.prompt: Read: 'The miniature toy car was so tiny it fit in my pocket.' Miniature means — (A) very small  (B) very colorful

steps: The clue is 'so tiny it fit in my pocket.'
Miniature means very small.

items.prompt: The word redo has the prefix re-. Redo means — (A) do something again  (B) do something for the first time

steps: re- means 'again.'
redo = do again.

items.prompt: Read: 'The ancient castle was built more than one thousand years ago.' Ancient means — (A) very old  (B) brand new

steps: The clue is 'built more than one thousand years ago.'
Ancient means very old.

items.prompt: The word dislike has the prefix dis-. Dislike means — (A) like very much  (B) not like

steps: The prefix dis- means 'not' or 'the opposite of.'
dislike = not like.

items.prompt: Read: 'The nutritious meal had vegetables, fruit, and whole grains — all things that are good for your body.' Nutritious means — (A) good for your health  (B) bad for your health

steps: The sentence lists healthy foods and says they are 'good for your body.'
Nutritious means good for your health.

items.prompt: The word helpful has the suffix -ful. Helpful means — (A) giving help  (B) needing help

steps: The suffix -ful means 'full of' or 'having the quality of.'
helpful = full of help, giving help.

items.prompt: Read: 'Ice will dissolve — no wait — it will melt in the warm sun. Sugar will dissolve in water and seem to disappear.' Dissolve means — (A) mix into a liquid and disappear  (B) freeze and become solid
items.answer: A — mix into a liquid and disappear

steps: The sentence says sugar 'dissolves in water and seems to disappear.'
Dissolve means to mix into a liquid until it is no longer visible.

items.prompt: The word careless has the suffix -less. Careless means — (A) full of care  (B) without care

steps: The suffix -less means 'without.'
careless = without care.

items.prompt: Read: 'The flexible gymnast could bend and stretch in many directions.' Flexible means — (A) able to bend easily  (B) unable to move

steps: The clue is 'could bend and stretch in many directions.'
Flexible means able to bend easily.

items.prompt: The word misplace has the prefix mis-. Misplace means — (A) put something in the wrong place  (B) put something in the right place
items.answer: A — put something in the wrong place

steps: mis- means 'wrongly' or 'badly.'
misplace = place wrongly, or put in the wrong spot.

items.prompt: Read: 'Glass is transparent, so you can see right through it.' Transparent means — (A) see-through  (B) very strong

steps: The clue is 'you can see right through it.'
Transparent means see-through.
